skills.description: Use Charmbracelet Gum to build polished interactive shell scripts with prompts, selectors, filters, spinners, formatting, tables, pagers, logging, and styled terminal output. Use when writing, reviewing, or debugging shell workflows that invoke the `gum` CLI.

Build, debug, and test terminal UIs and interactive CLIs with Ink (vadimdemedes/ink), "React for CLIs". Use this skill whenever the user mentions Ink, `ink` imports (`import {render, Box, Text} from 'ink'`), create-ink-app, ink-testing-library, or ink-* packages (ink-text-input, ink-spinner, ink-select-input), or wants to build a CLI/TUI/terminal dashboard/interactive prompt/spinner/progress UI/full-screen terminal app using React components, hooks, or Flexbox layout in the terminal, even if they never say "Ink" explicitly. Also use it for fixing Ink problems such as flickering output, app exiting immediately, useInput raw-mode errors, console.log mixing with the UI, text wrapping or layout issues, or testing Ink components.

Serena MCP for project memory and code navigation. Use when managing Serena memories, navigating symbols, performing intelligent refactoring, or maintaining context/continuity across AI agent sessions.

Inspect and manipulate a live, running Unreal Engine game through the ue4ss-bridge MCP server (UE4SS plus the UEBridge Lua mod). Use this whenever the user wants to examine UObjects, properties, UFunctions or class hierarchies in a running game; read or change a value live; run Lua inside the game; snapshot/diff or watch/hook values while they play; find out what the camera is aimed at; trigger UE4SS dumps (usmap, jmap, uht, cxx); or whenever ue4ss-bridge tools (bridge_status, inspect_object, eval_lua, snapshot_object, watch_property, hook_function, poll_events, etc.) are available. Also trigger on mentions of UE4SS, UEBridge, Unreal game modding or reverse engineering, "the player pawn/controller", or finding offsets and property names in a live game, even if the user never names the tool.
